finding: The recovery-evidence gap is narrower than before but is not closed. Public literature contains multiple experimental controllers and validated corrective-action cases, yet reusable row-level chronological datasets remain rare. The strongest new sources show explicit recovery horizons of 6 shots, 10-25 cycles, startup runs-to-quality reductions, autonomous next-cycle adjustments, and large-scale before/after factory validation.

strongestNewTargets.why: Measured induced disturbance, actual V/P/holding-pressure corrections and verified recovery within six shots.
16-cavity, five-material/vendor experiment with explicit material transitions, feedback action and 10/25-cycle recovery horizons plus physical dimensions.
Cross-machine and multi-viscosity startup tuning using vision defect acceptance with reported 88% lower runs-to-quality and 94% lower startup scrap.
2026 adaptive external-sensor study explicitly states data are available on request and includes appearance-defect optimization plus continuous adaptive weight control.
Real factory short-shot case with very large baseline and validation populations and verified production defect-rate reduction from about 1.2% to 0.32%.
Clean physical flash defect -> DOE diagnosis -> parameter correction -> consecutive zero-flash confirmation runs.

remainingCriticalGapDefinition.requiredGrain: one row/event sequence per chronological production shot or small run block

whatChangedAfter200Passes: There is now substantially stronger publisher-verified evidence that shot/cycle-level recovery experiments exist across multiple independent research groups.
The search surfaced explicit recovery horizons rather than only steady-state quality improvements.
A large fraction of the best evidence is still trapped in figures, tables, confidential files or author-held datasets rather than downloadable machine-readable chronological tables.
Several NCKU/Hwang adaptive-control papers form a shared lineage and must be de-duplicated at experiment level before any independence count is increased.
Generic searching now has very low expected value relative to direct author/industrial data requests and exact-file admission work.
